tip.title: One effect becomes the next cause
tip.text: In science and history texts, causes often form a CHAIN: A causes B, B causes C. To follow a chain, draw arrows as you read. Also watch for several causes of one effect, or one cause with several effects. Be careful: two things happening one after the other does not always mean the first caused the second. Look for the words that prove the link: because, leads to, results in, due to, therefore.

passage.title: The Coral and the Fisherman
passage.text:
In the warm shallow waters around many Philippine islands lie coral reefs, built over centuries by tiny animals called polyps. Each polyp makes a hard skeleton, and millions of skeletons together form the reef. Inside the polyps live even tinier algae that give the coral its color and, through sunlight, most of its food.

When the sea becomes unusually warm, even by one or two degrees, the polyps become stressed and push the algae out. Without the algae, the coral turns ghostly white. Scientists call this bleaching. A bleached coral is not dead yet, but it is starving. If the water stays warm for weeks, the coral dies.

The damage does not stop there. Reefs are where small fish feed and hide. As the coral dies, the small fish disappear, and the larger fish that eat them move away or die too. Fishermen who once filled their boats near the reef come home with little. Some switch to dynamite fishing to catch what is left, which shatters more coral, leaving even fewer places for fish to live.

The chain can also run the other way. When communities protect a reef by banning destructive fishing and reducing pollution, the coral recovers, the small fish return, the big fish follow, and catches rise again.

words.meaning: tiny soft sea animals that build coral
words.example: A reef is made by millions of polyps.

words.meaning: coral turning white after losing its algae because of stress
words.example: Warm seas caused coral bleaching this summer.
The destructive typhoon flattened the crops.

items.prompt: "In the warm shallow waters around many Philippine islands lie coral reefs." What does lie mean here?
choices: To say something untrue
To be located or rest in a place
To lay an egg
To stay in bed
items.why: The sentence tells where the reefs are found, so lie means to be located there, not to tell an untruth.

items.prompt: What causes coral to turn white?
choices: Too much sunlight on the water
Polyps pushing out their algae when the water gets too warm
Fish eating the color
Dynamite fishing
items.why: "The polyps become stressed and push the algae out. Without the algae, the coral turns ghostly white."

items.prompt: Why does a bleached coral starve?
choices: Fish stop feeding it.
The algae that made most of its food are gone.
The water is too cold.
Fishermen take its food.
items.why: The algae give the coral "most of its food." Without them, the coral has nothing to eat.

choices: Scientists call white coral bleaching.
Coral is beautiful and should be protected.
A bleached coral is already dead.
Warm water makes polyps push out their algae, so the coral turns white and starves, and it dies if the warmth lasts for weeks.
items.why: Choice D keeps the cause, the bleaching, and the result. Choice A is one detail, choice B is an opinion the paragraph never states, and choice C contradicts "not dead yet."

items.prompt: Arrange this chain of causes and effects in order.
steps: Small fish lose their feeding and hiding places.
items.why: Each effect becomes the next cause: warm water leads to coral death, then small fish, then large fish, then the catch.

items.prompt: How does dynamite fishing make the problem WORSE?
choices: It warms the water.
It shatters more coral, leaving fewer places for fish.
It feeds the polyps.
It brings in more fishermen.
items.why: "...which shatters more coral, leaving even fewer places for fish to live."

choices: When coral dies, the fish leave, fishermen catch less, and some turn to dynamite fishing, which destroys even more coral.
Fishermen should stop using dynamite.
Small fish feed and hide in the reef.
Fishermen once filled their boats near the reef.
items.why: Choice A follows the whole chain in the paragraph. Choice B is advice the text does not give, and choices C and D are single details.

items.prompt: "The chain can also run the other way." What does run mean here?
choices: To move fast on foot
To manage a shop or business
To go or work in a certain direction
To leak or drip
items.why: The next sentence shows the same chain of events happening in reverse, so run means to go in a direction.

items.prompt: "...the big fish follow, and catches rise again." What does catches mean here?
choices: Hooks or locks on a door
Hidden problems in a deal
Grabs made with the hands
The amounts of fish caught
items.why: The paragraph is about fishermen, so catches means the fish they bring home. Earlier, fishermen "come home with little."

items.prompt: Which is the BEST summary of the whole passage?
choices: Polyps build reefs and algae give them color.
Dynamite fishing is the main reason fish are disappearing.
Warm seas bleach and kill coral, which drives away the fish and the fishermen's catches, but protecting a reef can reverse the chain.
Filipino fishermen are poor because of warm water.
items.why: Choice C covers the cause, the chain of effects, and the recovery in the last paragraph. Choice A is only the opening, and choices B and D claim more than the text says.
